meta.title: The eight stages of a cold call
meta.derived_from: 100 rewritten cold-call transcripts + the supplied stage sheet
meta.note: CONTENT_PENDING_TRANSCRIPT_ANALYSIS — placeholder structure, replaced after reading the supplied transcripts.

stages.name: Open
stages.purpose: Get a few seconds of attention and permission to keep talking, without sounding like a pitch.
caller_does: Say the name and why you are calling in one breath

prospects_say.mean: They are screening, not rejecting. Name the company, not the product.

prospects_say.line: I'm in the middle of something.
prospects_say.mean: Asking for a cost, not saying no. Offer a time cost of under a minute.

stages.watch_out: Talking for more than 12 seconds before they have said a word.

stages.name: Reason for the call
stages.purpose: Say why them, why now, in one sentence they could repeat to a colleague.
caller_does: Name something specific to their business

prospects_say.line: How did you get my number?
prospects_say.mean: They want provenance before content. Answer in five words and move on.

prospects_say.line: We already have someone for that.
prospects_say.mean: Open to the category, closed to a swap. Ask what they would change about it.

stages.watch_out: Describing your product instead of their situation.

stages.name: Ask permission
stages.purpose: Trade a question for a moment of their time so the rest of the call is theirs, not yours.
caller_does: Accept 'no' gracefully if they will not give it

prospects_say.mean: A real door. Honour it out loud and the next stage gets easier.

prospects_say.line: Just tell me what it is.
prospects_say.mean: They want the shape of it first. Give one line, then ask the question.

stages.watch_out: Asking permission twice — the second one sounds like a script.

stages.name: Find the problem
stages.purpose: Get them to say the thing that is costing them, in their words, not yours.
caller_does: Say nothing for four seconds after they answer

prospects_say.line: We're fine with how it works now.
prospects_say.mean: Default answer. Ask what changed this year, or what they would fix if free.
Priorities are about timing. Ask what would have to be true for it to become one.

stages.watch_out: Jumping to the pitch the moment they mention any discomfort.

stages.name: Reframe
stages.purpose: Connect their problem to a way of fixing it, so your product arrives as an answer rather than a pitch.
caller_does: Offer one outcome, not five features

prospects_say.mean: They are close enough to price it. Give a range and ask if that is in range.
Sometimes a brush-off, sometimes real. Ask what line in the email would make them open it.

stages.watch_out: A feature list. One problem, one outcome, one number.

stages.name: Handle the pushback
stages.purpose: Let the objection be said fully, then answer the actual one instead of the one you expected.
caller_does: Name the objection out loud before answering it

prospects_say.mean: About today, not the product. Ask when a good time is and mean it.
Often a priority statement. Ask what would justify the budget rather than cutting the number.

stages.watch_out: Answering the objection before they have finished saying it.

stages.name: Prove it
stages.purpose: Give one piece of evidence they can check, sized to the thirty seconds you have left.
caller_does: Use one comparable customer or number
Offer the proof in the follow-up, not the pitch

prospects_say.mean: They are testing whether you are real. One name beats three logos.

prospects_say.line: I'd have to look into it.
prospects_say.mean: They have no reason to believe the effort is theirs. Offer to send the two things they would look at.

stages.watch_out: Promising a case study you then fail to send.

stages.name: Ask for the meeting
stages.purpose: Convert the conversation into a next step with a day and a time attached to it.
caller_does: Confirm it before you hang up

prospects_say.line: What do I need to do?
prospects_say.mean: They want the mechanics. Answer with a calendar move, not a website link.
Rarely means yes. Offer the smallest next step: ten minutes, their calendar, this week.

stages.watch_out: Ending on 'I'll follow up' with no date attached to either side.

outcomes.label: Meeting booked
outcomes.meta: A slot was agreed before the call ended.

outcomes.label: Follow-up agreed
outcomes.meta: They asked to be contacted, with no meeting set.

outcomes.label: Not right now
outcomes.meta: Interested, wrong moment. Worth a dated retry.

outcomes.label: Not a fit
outcomes.meta: Company, size or need does not match what you sell.

outcomes.label: Wrong person
outcomes.meta: Someone else owns this. Ask for the name before you hang up.

outcomes.label: Refused outright
outcomes.meta: Ended the call. Do not dial this number again this quarter.

outcomes.label: No answer / voicemail
outcomes.meta: Reached nobody. The stage trail stops where it stopped.
